newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Codelco says Asia to form backbone of sales.
newsitem.headline: Codelco says Asia to form backbone of sales.

text.p: Robust Asian copper demand will form the backbone of sales for Chilean mining giant Codelco over the next few years, the general manager of its second biggest mine said on Tuesday.

"For all of our business, Asia is our future," Fernando Riveri, general manager of Codelco's El Teniente mine, told reporters at a briefing. He was in Singapore for the signing of a copper smelter agreement with a Thai company.
The Chilean company will help operate the smelter in a deal worth US$50 million over the next three years, Riveri said.
The Codelco official said production in El Teniente, second only in size to the massive Chuquicamata open pit mine, should reach 350,000 tonnes for calendar 1996.
Output at El Teniente in the first nine months of the year reached only 252,600 tonnes against 238,000 tonnes in the same period last year.
Total production last year at El Teniente reached 322,000 tonnes and Codelco had earlier forecast that output in 1996 will range between 342,000-360,000 tonnes.
Codelco's total production for 1996 is expected to touch 1.5 million tonnes.
The company is pursuing three projects in Asia on which it hopes to conclude an agreement in the first half of 1997, Riveri said, declining to elaborate on the companies or countries involved.
Codelco will sign on Wednesday an agreement to provide technical expertise in the startup of the Rayong copper smelter of Thai Copper Industries Ltd.
"We are very sure of 350,000 tonnes this year. We hope to produce 350,0000 tonnes in 1997," he said. "We don't have any problems for November and December."
He forecast that copper prices in 1997 will range between $0.90 to $0.95 a lb, although he would prefer $1.00 a lb.
Asked if the price next year is adequate for Codelco, he said: "Ninety-five cents is a good price for us."
